item.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
item.description: Right now, there is probably an AI agent running on a laptop somewhere in your network.

item.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
item.description:
Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.
The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator privileges, the top level of control over it.

item.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
item.description: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority (CA), will withdraw from its global SSL/TLS certificate business, its board decided on Thursday. The decision came five days after a researcher reported recovering the private keys of eight of its intermediate CA certificates.

item.title: ThreatsDay: AI Secrets Leak, PingCAP Source Theft, Signal Hang-Up Flaw, Laravel Auth Bypass + 21 More
item.description: This week has already been rough for cybersecurity.

item.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE Flaws Disclosed on Public Mailing Lists Before Kernel Fixes
item.description:
Linux servers running KSMBD, the kernel's built-in SMB server, are exposed to two publicly reported remote code execution flaws rated 9.0 by Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative, with no fix yet in the mainline kernel.
One of them, ZDI-CAN-33774, can be triggered before any network authentication.

item.title: INTERPOL Arrests 1,462 Suspects, Disrupts 10,909 Cybercrime Networks in Global Crackdown
item.description: INTERPOL on Thursday announced that a coordinated law enforcement action has disrupted 10,909 malicious networks and recovered more than $105 million in illicit funds. Codenamed Operation Serengeti III, the cybercrime crackdown took place between June 29 and August 31, 2026.

item.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
item.description: Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) provider Railway on Wednesday disclosed "anomalous activity" related to systems that store customer environment variables. An unauthorized third party may have gained access to encrypted environment variables, and, in some cases, obtained the decrypted contents.

item.title: LiteLLM Suspects GitHub Token Leak in AI Gateway Logs Behind Malicious Package Release
item.description: LiteLLM on Wednesday disclosed that threat actors compromised "multiple independent security controls" to push a malicious version of the Python package containing a credential stealer and a backdoor. On October 21, 2026, LiteLLM's release pipeline was compromised to push 1.107.0 to the Docker Hub registry and the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository.

item.title: Node.js Brotli Decoder Bug Could Allow Remote Code Execution in All Supported Versions
item.description: Node.js released security updates on October 21 for its three supported release lines, 22.x, 24.x and 26.x, fixing 10 flaws. The most serious is a bug in the Brotli decompression code that Node.js bundles, which the project says can allow remote code execution.

item.title: New QPACK Flaws Can Crash HTTP/3 Servers, Trigger Up to 4,000-Fold Memory Amplification
item.description: A remote attacker who has not logged in can crash many HTTP/3 web servers with a single connection, security firm FoxIO disclosed, releasing working proof-of-concept code.

item.title: Someone Tried to Exploit PHP2Shell 4 Days Before the Vulnerabilities Were Publicly Disclosed
item.description: Amazon's Threat Intelligence team on Wednesday said it detected an attempt to exploit the newly disclosed PHP2Shell vulnerabilities dating back to October 17, 2026, against its MadPot honeypot service, as the flaws come under broad exploitation in the wild following the release of the patches.

item.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
item.description: Microsoft on Wednesday disclosed that a China state-aligned actor dubbed Storm-0940 was behind the recent supply chain compromise of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application.

item.title: Critical GitLab Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Could Allow Unauthenticated RCE Across 12 Years of Releases
item.description: GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014. The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier.

item.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Delivering Credential Stealer and Backdoor
item.description: The popular LiteLLM Python package has been compromised as part of a software supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and a backdoor. The compromise affects LiteLLM 1.107.0, distributed through PyPI wheels and Docker images.

item.title: PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge
item.description: PHP has released emergency updates that fix two critical flaws in the language itself, letting an attacker without an account run code on a web server. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the PHP team says only updating fully protects a server.

item.title: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
item.description: Google on Tuesday said it's rolling out improved safeguards in its Chrome browser to secure users against ClickFix attacks when Enhanced Protection is enabled.

item.title: Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
item.description: Attackers took control of more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and used them to redirect SSH connections to servers that stole login passwords, a researcher found.

item.title: Attackers Abuse UpdraftCentral Keys to Plant Backdoors on WordPress Sites
item.description: Unknown threat actors breached TeamUpdraft's website and potentially gained unauthorized access to customers' connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone, using them to backdoor WordPress sites.

item.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Exploited Plex2Shell, Siemens, and SiteGuard Flaws
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including four vulnerabilities impacting Plex Media Server that's collectively called Plex2Shell.

item.title: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
item.description: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates are compromised, Mozilla and Google's Chrome Root Program confirms on October 20. An intermediate CA signs the certificates that websites present, so anyone holding one of these keys could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept.

item.title: Critical FortiSIEM Flaw Gets Public Exploit PoC for Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have released a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for a recently patched critical security flaw impacting Fortinet FortiSIEM that could result in arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS score: 9.4), is a critical path traversal flaw.

item.title: Qilin and INC Ransomware Groups Exploit Palo Alto Networks Flaw to Bypass MFA
item.description: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed that it's continuing to observe exploitation of a now-patched security flaw impacting  PAN-OS and Prisma Access by ransomware actors. The activity relates to CVE-2026-0257 (CVSS score: 7.8), an authentication bypass flaw that could be exploited to set up unauthorized VPN connections.
